inline_comments.comment: The underline character for 'Selecting a part of a trajectory' is dots (`....`), but every other peer section in this file uses dashes (`---`). In RST, section hierarchy is determined by the order decoration characters are first encountered after the title. Because `....` appears before `---`, Sphinx assigns dots to level 1 and dashes to level 2, which means 'Basic controls', 'Plotting data from the command line', 'Configuring the GUI', and 'Polling the GUI' are all rendered as *subsections of* 'Selecting a part of a trajectory' rather than independent siblings of it. Change this underline to `---` to match the rest of the file and restore the intended flat structure.

The line `.. or` is an RST comment (anything starting with `..` followed by a space is a comment if not a known directive). It produces no rendered output and, together with the commented-out line `.. >>> view(atoms, repeat=(3, 3, 2))` immediately below, silently hides the `repeat` example that was present in the previous version of this page. If `repeat` is intentionally being removed, delete these lines entirely; if it should remain as an example, uncomment it (remove the leading `..`).

The anchor `.. _gui-tools graphs:` contains a space, making it the only anchor in this diff that is not fully hyphenated. Every other anchor introduced (`.. _gui-view:`, `.. _gui-edit:`, `.. _gui-setup:`, `.. _gui-tools movie:`) uses hyphens consistently. Consider renaming it to `.. _gui-tools-graphs:` (and updating the corresponding `:ref:` in `basics.rst`) for consistency. RST does allow spaces in label names, but the cross-reference syntax `:ref:`gui-tools graphs`` looks unusual compared to the rest.

The NEB interpolation CLI example has been silently commented out using RST comment syntax (`.. ::` / `..   $ ase gui --interpolate ...`). The two lines produce no rendered output, so readers of the NEB plot section get no concrete usage example. If the `--interpolate` flag is broken or deprecated, say so explicitly in the prose. If it still works, restore the example as a proper `::` code block.

All nine changed menu label strings (e.g. `'Show _Labels'` → `'Show _labels'`, `'Quick Info ...'` → `'Quick info ...'`, etc.) are passed through `_()` for gettext localisation, which uses the string's exact content as the translation lookup key. Changing capitalisation silently invalidates any existing `.po`/`.mo` translation entries for these strings; translated GUIs will fall back to the English text. If translations are maintained for the project (even partially), coordinate this change with the translation team or regenerate the translation template.

The blank line between the `.. attention::` directive marker and its content body (line 6 in the new file) contains four trailing spaces. While RST may still render the block correctly, the trailing whitespace will fail many lint/CI checks. Remove the spaces so the line is truly blank.
Grammar error: "Depending on **you** operating system" should be "Depending on **your** operating system".

general_comments.comment: The 'Writing files' section has been removed from `basics.rst` with no replacement anywhere in the diff. That section documented the `-o` flag for writing GUI output from the command line and listed the supported output formats (`traj`, `xyz`, `cube`, `pdb`, `eps`, `png`, `pov`). Users who want to know how to save structures from the CLI (`ase gui -n -1 a*.traj -o new.traj`) have no entry point into this information in the reorganised docs. Either restore the content under an appropriate heading in `basics.rst` or move it to the relevant menu page (e.g., under a 'File' menu description).
